title: English Sectional (75 Day Practice Mix) — Mock #36

questions.q_en:
Mental health has increasingly entered public discourse, yet its inclusion often remains superficial rather than transformative. Awareness campaigns proliferate, terminology becomes more familiar, and institutions adopt symbolic gestures of concern. However, beneath this apparent progress lies a persistent reluctance to confront the structural and cultural conditions that generate psychological distress. Mental health is frequently treated as an individual malfunction, detached from social environments that normalize chronic stress, insecurity, and emotional suppression. This individualized framing carries subtle consequences. When distress is reduced to personal resilience or chemical imbalance, responsibility quietly shifts away from workplaces, educational systems, and economic arrangements that perpetuate exhaustion and precarity. Coping mechanisms are emphasized over prevention, and adaptation is rewarded more than dissent. In such a framework, the mentally healthy individual is not one who is free from distress, but one who can continue functioning despite it. Institutional responses often mirror this logic. Support systems exist, but access is conditional, fragmented, and reactive. Interventions are triggered once productivity declines or visible crisis emerges, rather than when early signs of strain appear. Moreover, the language of wellness is frequently co-opted to enhance performance rather than well-being, blurring the line between care and control. As a result, mental health initiatives risk becoming tools for sustaining existing norms rather than questioning them. The deeper challenge, therefore, lies in redefining mental health beyond the absence of disorder. It demands recognition of emotional suffering as a rational response to irrational conditions. Without this shift, societies may continue to expand mental health services while simultaneously reproducing the very pressures that make such services indispensable.

Which of the following would be the most appropriate title for the passage?

questions.q_en:
The following sentence contains a blank space, followed by four alternative options. You are required to choose the most appropriate option (A, B, C, or D) that grammatically completes the sentence in accordance with the rules of English grammar.

The constitutional amendment stipulates that the state _________ provide free and compulsory education to all children between the ages of six and fourteen.
questions.q_hi:
The following sentence contains a blank space, followed by four alternative options. You are required to choose the most appropriate option (A, B, C, or D) that grammatically completes the sentence in accordance with the rules of English grammar.

The constitutional amendment stipulates that the state _________ provide free and compulsory education to all children between the ages of six and fourteen.
questions.solution_en:
The correct answer is (c) shall.

The Rule: "Shall" for Official Mandates –

In formal English, particularly within legal statutes, constitutional provisions, or official directives, the modal verb "shall" is used with third-person subjects (he, she, it, they, or nouns like "the state") to express a mandatory command or a legal obligation.

Unlike "will," which merely predicts a future event, or "should," which often implies a suggestion or piece of advice, "shall" creates a binding requirement that must be followed.

Application to the Sentence - The sentence refers to a "constitutional amendment". "The state" is a third-person subject. The sentence is not just predicting that education will be provided; it is stating a law that mandates the state to provide it.

questions.q_en: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
questions.q_hi: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options_en: Our organization has consistently and will continue to provide
high-quality healthcare services to the underprivileged sections of society
as part of our long-term commitment to corporate social responsibility in this region.
No Error
options_hi: Our organization has consistently and will continue to provide
high-quality healthcare services to the underprivileged sections of society
as part of our long-term commitment to corporate social responsibility in this region.
No Error
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (A).

Replace “has consistently and will” with “has consistently provided and will”.

📌 Rule / Concept: Parallelism of Main Verbs with Different Auxiliaries -

When two auxiliary verbs (like has, have, had, will, can, must) are used in a sentence and they require different forms of the main verb, the main verb must be explicitly mentioned for each auxiliary.

Has/Have/Had requires the Past Participle (V3).

Will/Shall/Can/May requires the Base Form (V1).

If you use only one verb at the end, it must be grammatically compatible with both auxiliaries. If it isn't (e.g., has + provide is wrong), you must provide the correct form for each

💢 Application to the Given Question - In this sentence, the auxiliary "has" needs a V3 (provided), while "will continue" is followed by an infinitive (to provide). By omitting the verb after "has," the sentence implies "has provide," which is grammatically incorrect. To be accurate, you must add the V3 form after "has."

Corrected Sentence - Our organization has consistently provided and will continue to provide high-quality healthcare services to the underprivileged sections of society as part of our long-term commitment to corporate social responsibility in this region.

questions.q_en: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
questions.q_hi: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options_en: As soon as the mother had
laid the infant in the crib, she
lay down to rest her aching back.
No Error
options_hi: As soon as the mother had
laid the infant in the crib, she
lay down to rest her aching back.
No Error
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (D) - No Error.

Rule / Concept: Confusing Pairs of Verbs (Lie vs. Lay)

Lay (Transitive): Means "to put or place something." It requires a direct object.

Forms: Lay (V1) — Laid (V2) — Laid (V3).

Lie (Intransitive): Means "to recline or rest." It cannot take a direct object.

Forms: Lie (V1) — Lay (V2) — Lain (V3).

The Trap: The Past Tense (V2) of 'Lie' is 'Lay', which is identical to the Base Form (V1) of 'Lay'. Examiners use this overlap to confuse students.

💢 Application to the Given Question -

1. "had laid the infant": Here, "the infant" is the direct object. We need the V3 (Past Participle) form of the transitive verb Lay. Laid is perfectly correct.

2. "she lay down": Here, the subject (she) is reclining. There is no object. Since the first part of the sentence establishes a past context ("had laid"), we need the V2 (Past Tense) of the intransitive verb Lie. The V2 of Lie is Lay.

Both verbs have been used in their correct forms according to their respective roles in the sentence.

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate phrasal verb to fill in the blank.

The minister __________ the citizens to remain calm during the crisis.
questions.q_hi:
Select the most appropriate phrasal verb to fill in the blank.

The minister __________ the citizens to remain calm during the crisis
questions.solution_en:
Explanation: The correct answer is option (3).

English Explanation: “Call upon” means to formally request, appeal to, or urge someone to do something. In the sentence, the minister is formally urging the citizens to remain calm during the crisis. Therefore, “called upon” correctly conveys the idea of making an official or formal appeal. “Call off” means to cancel something. “Call in” means to summon someone (often for help or questioning). “Call for” means to demand or require something. Since the context involves a formal appeal directed at people, “called upon” is the most appropriate fit.

1. Called off (रद्द कर देना)
Example: The match was called off due to heavy rain. (भारी बारिश के कारण मैच रद्द कर दिया गया।)

2. Called in (बुलाना / तलब करना)
Example: The manager called in the staff for an urgent meeting. (प्रबंधक ने कर्मचारियों को तुरंत बैठक के लिए बुलाया।)

3. Called upon (औपचारिक रूप से आग्रह करना)
Example: The chairman called upon all members to maintain discipline during the meeting. (अध्यक्ष ने सभी सदस्यों से बैठक में अनुशासन बनाए रखने का आग्रह किया।)

4. Called for (मांग करना / आवश्यकता होना)
Example: The situation calls for immediate action. (स्थिति तत्काल कार्रवाई की मांग करती है।)

questions.q_en:
Identify whether the highlighted group of words is a phrase or a clause.

The manager postponed the meeting because several important documents were still missing.
questions.q_hi:
Identify whether the highlighted group of words is a phrase or a clause.

The manager postponed the meeting because several important documents were still missing.
questions.solution_en:
Answer: C) Clause

Explanation: A clause is a group of words that contain both a subject and a verb. A phrase does not contain a complete subject-verb combination.

In the highlighted part:

“several important documents” = subject, “were” = verb

Since the group contains both a subject and a verb, it is a clause.

questions.q_en:
Select the passive form of the given sentence.
The authorities will have completed the forensic analysis before presenting the final report.
questions.q_hi:
Select the passive form of the given sentence.
The authorities will have completed the forensic analysis before presenting the final repor
options_en: The forensic analysis will be completed before presenting the final report.
The forensic analysis will have been completed before presenting the final report.
No passive form is possible.
The forensic analysis has been completed before presenting the final report.
options_hi: The forensic analysis will be completed before presenting the final report.
The forensic analysis will have been completed before presenting the final report.
No passive form is possible.
The forensic analysis has been completed before presenting the final report.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (B)

📌 Rule / Concept: Future Perfect Tense – Active to Passive Conversion

In the Future Perfect tense, the active structure is:
Subject + will have + V³ + Object

The passive structure becomes:

Object + will have + been + V³ (+ by + Subject)

The word “been” is compulsory in Future Perfect passive constructions. The tense must remain Future Perfect after conversion.

Here, “will have completed” is in Future Perfect tense.
“The forensic analysis” is the object and becomes the subject in passive voice. In Future Perfect passive, we must use “will have been” + V³. The verb “completed” remains in its past participle form.

Hence, “will have been completed” is the correct transformation.

questions.q_en: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
questions.q_hi: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options_en: Regular morning meditation helps students
improving their concentration and memory,
especially when they are preparing for competitive exams.
options_hi: Regular morning meditation helps students
improving their concentration and memory,
especially when they are preparing for competitive exams.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (B) Replace “improving” with “improve” or “to improve”

📌 Rule / Concept: Verbs after "Help"

The verb "Help" follows a unique pattern in English grammar. It can be followed by an object and then either a Bare Infinitive (V1 without "to") or a Full Infinitive (to + V1). Both are grammatically acceptable and carry the same meaning. However, "Help" is never followed by a Gerund (V+Ing)

💢 Application to the Given Question

"...helps students improving their concentration..."

In this sentence, the verb "helps" is followed by the object "students." The secondary action "improving" is currently in the gerund/participle form ($-ing$). According to the rule, this must be changed to the base form "improve" or the infinitive "to improve" to be grammatically correct.

Corrected Sentence

Regular morning meditation helps students improve (or to improve) their concentration and memory, especially when they are preparing competitive exams .

More Examples for Clarity

Example 1 ✅ Could you help me carry these heavy boxes to the car?

Example 2 ✅ This ointment will help the wound to heal faster.

Example 3 ✅ The teacher helped the children solve the difficult puzzle.

questions.q_en: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
questions.q_hi: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options_en: The military commander strictly ordered
the rebellious soldiers to lay down
their arms or to face a court-martial.
options_hi: The military commander strictly ordered
the rebellious soldiers to lay down
their arms or to face a court-martial.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (C) Replace “to face” with “face”.

📌 Rule / Concept: Parallelism in Infinitives

When two or more infinitives are joined by a coordinating conjunction (such as and, or, but, except, than), the second infinitive usually drops the "to" marker. This is known as Ellipsis—the omission of a word that is already understood from the first part of the sentence. In competitive exams like SSC CGL and Banking, repeating the "to" is considered redundant and a violation of the rule of parallelism.

💢 Application to the Given Question

"...to lay down their arms or to face a court-martial."

In this sentence, the verb "ordered" governs two actions: to lay down and to face. Since both actions are part of the same command and are connected by the conjunction "or," the "to" before "face" is unnecessary and should be removed to maintain a parallel and concise structure.

Corrected Sentence

The military commander strictly ordered the rebellious soldiers to lay down their arms or face a court-martial.

More Examples for Clarity

Example 1 ✅ I would rather die than beg. (Note: "than" follows this rule strictly).

Example 2 ✅ She helped me to carry the bags and open the door.

Example 3 ✅ The goal is to learn from mistakes and grow as an individual.

English Explanation: “Do away with” means to abolish, eliminate, or remove something completely. In the sentence, the management plans to remove the outdated attendance policy entirely. Therefore, “do away with” correctly conveys the idea of completely abolishing a rule. “Do without” means to manage in the absence of something. “Do up” means to decorate, fasten, or renovate something. “Do over” means to repeat or redo something. Since the context involves permanently removing a policy, “do away with” is the most appropriate fit.

1. Do without (बिना किसी चीज़ के काम चलाना)
Example: We will have to do without extra staff this month. (हमें इस महीने अतिरिक्त कर्मचारियों के बिना काम चलाना पड़ेगा।)

2. Do away with (समाप्त कर देना / खत्म करना)
Example : The company decided to do away with unnecessary paperwork. (कंपनी ने अनावश्यक कागज़ी कार्यवाही को समाप्त कर दिया।)
3. Do up (सजाना / मरम्मत करना / बंद करना)
Example: They plan to do up the old house before selling it. (वे पुराने घर को बेचने से पहले उसकी मरम्मत करेंगे।)

4. Do over (दोबारा करना)
Example: The teacher asked him to do the assignment over. (शिक्षक ने उसे कार्य दोबारा करने को कहा।)

The king said to his messenger, "Come hither immediately."

The king said to his messenger, "Come hither immediately."
options_en: The king ordered his messenger to go there immediately.
The king ordered his messenger to come thither immediately.
The king ordered his messenger to go thither immediately.
The king ordered his messenger to come hither immediately.
options_hi: The king ordered his messenger to go there immediately.
The king ordered his messenger to come thither immediately.
The king ordered his messenger to go thither immediately.
The king ordered his messenger to come hither immediately.
questions.solution_en:
The correct answer is Option C: The king ordered his messenger to go thither immediately.

Key Points

  • The Rare Word Change: In narration, words showing "nearness" change to words showing "distance."

    • Hither (to this place) becomes Thither (to that place).

  • Verb Change (Come to Go): When "come" is used with a word of nearness like "hither," it often changes to "go" in indirect speech to reflect the change in perspective from the speaker's location.

  • Reporting Verb: Since it is a command, "said to" changes to "ordered".

  • Infinitive Connector: For imperative sentences (commands), we use "to + verb" to connect the speech.

questions.q_en: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
questions.q_hi: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options_en: The local residents have terrified of the frequent
leopard sightings in the area since the beginning
of the monsoon season this year.
options_hi: The local residents have terrified of the frequent
leopard sightings in the area since the beginning
of the monsoon season this year.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (A) Replace “have” with “have been”.

📌 Rule / Concept: use of passive verb form in the tense structure

Use passive verb form structure when receiver is subject of the sentence.

💢 Application to the Given Question

"...The local residents have terrified of the frequent leopard sightings..."

In this sentence, "terrified" is an adjective describing the residents.

  • If you say "have terrified," the sentence becomes active, meaning the residents scared someone else.

  • To show that the residents are themselves in a state of terror since a point in the past (the monsoon), you must use "have been terrified.

Corrected Sentence

The local residents have been terrified of the frequent leopard sightings in the area since the beginning of the monsoon season this year.

options_en:

would be

will be

is
options_hi:
would have been

would be

will be

is
questions.solution_en:
✅ Correct Answer - would be

📌 Rule / Concept: Mixed Conditional (Past Unreal Condition → Present Result)

This sentence tests a mixed conditional, where:

  • The if-clause refers to an unreal past condition
  • The main clause refers to a present consequence

Core Structure:  If + had + past participle → would + base verb

Step-by-step logic:

  1. “had been trained”
    • Past perfect → confirms a hypothetical past situation
    • The training did not happen as required
  2. “today”
    • Explicit present-time marker
    • Forces the result clause to describe a current state
  3. Therefore, the result must be:
    • would + base verb → would be

NOT would have been (which would wrongly shift the result into the past)

questions.q_en: Each of the applicants has fulfilled the eligibility criteria, ______?
questions.q_hi: Each of the applicants has fulfilled the eligibility criteria, ______?
options_en: haven’t they
hasn’t he
didn’t they
hasn’t they
options_hi: haven’t they
hasn’t he
didn’t they
hasn’t they
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (B) - “hasn’t he”.

📌 Rule / Concept: “Each of” + Singular Agreement in Question Tags

When a sentence begins with: Each of + plural noun

The grammatical subject is “each”, not the plural noun.

“Each” is singular, so:

  • The verb must be singular

  • The tag pronoun must also be singular

In traditional formal competitive exams, the singular pronoun “he” is preferred in tags.

💢 Application to the Given Question

Each of the applicants has fulfilled the eligibility criteria

  • Real subject = Each (singular)

  • Verb used = has (correct singular auxiliary)

  • Statement is positive → tag must be negative

  • Pronoun must agree with “each” → singular

Therefore: hasn’t he?

✅ More Examples for Clarity

Example 1 ✅- Each of the students has submitted the form, hasn’t he?

Example 2 ✅- Each of the officers was present, wasn’t he?

Example 3 ✅- Each of the candidates has cleared the test, hasn’t he?

🧠 Things to Remember

  • “Each of” → subject is singular.

  • Ignore the plural noun after “of”.

  • Verb and tag must be singular.

  • SSC usually prefers singular pronoun in such cases.

questions.q_en:
As digital platforms increasingly mediate everyday interactions, concerns over data privacy have moved from technical circles to the center of public debate. Corporations often justify extensive data collection as necessary for personalization and efficiency, yet critics argue that such practices frequently [---1---] user consent by embedding permissions within complex terms of service. Moreover, the aggregation of personal data across platforms can lead to [---2---] surveillance, where individuals are monitored without explicit awareness. When data breaches occur, institutional responses are often [----3----], focusing on damage control rather than structural reform. Experts therefore contend that meaningful data protection requires a [----4----] shift toward user-centric governance and enforceable accountability.

Choose the most appropriate option to fill in the blank [1] :

Moreover, the aggregation of personal data across platforms can lead to [---2---] surveillance, where individuals are monitored without explicit awareness. When data breaches occur, institutional responses are often [----3----], focusing on damage control rather than structural reform. Experts therefore contend that meaningful data protection requires a [----4----] shift toward user-centric governance and enforceable accountability.

Choose the most appropriate option to fill in the blank [1] :
options_en: reinforce
circumvent
authenticate
formalize
options_hi: reinforce
circumvent
authenticate
formalize
questions.solution_en:
Circumvent means to bypass or avoid something indirectly. The passage suggests that consent is technically obtained but effectively undermined through complexity, making circumvent the most accurate choice.
WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE WRONG
• Reinforce implies strengthening consent, not weakening it.
• Authenticate means verify authenticity, irrelevant here.
• Formalize suggests making procedures official, not evasive.
